newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen mixed, awaiting rate clues.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen mixed, awaiting rate clues.

text.p: U.S. stocks are expected to open mixed, with investors awaiting the release of August housing starts and weekly jobless claims for further clues about the future of interest rates.

Housing starts, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, are expected to show an annual rate of 1.445 million in August, compared with 1.46 million in July. Weekly jobless claims are expected to edge lower, to 335,000 from 338,000 in the previous week.
The Philadelphia Fed Survey is due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
Economists are predicting a decline in all three reports. The data are expected to support the bond and stock markets.

"I don't think the numbers will throw off the opening if they come in on target," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood. "I expect this fixation on interest rates will cool off for a while. People will take a wait-and-see approach to what's going to happen at the Fed meeting next week."

Peter Cardillo, Westfalia Investments director of research, said, "Housing starts and initial jobless claims will probably direct the market, but techs could drag on the opening, based on the sell-off going on now in London."
He added, "Any large decline in initial jobess claims could also dampen the stock market and accelerate a selloff, but I don't really expect that."
Standard & Poor's futures rose 1.10 to 688.30. The long bond was up four ticks to yield 7.01 percent ahead of the start of trading.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column said Dexter Corp was being pressed to unlock the value of its majority stake in Life Technologies Inc.
